analysis.title: US (Post-)Election Curveballs: Should Investors Worry?
key_insights: TS Lombard maps three asymmetric waves of electoral risk: Wave 1 around Election Day (1-8 Nov), Wave 2 state vote certifications (6 Nov to mid-Dec), Wave 3 the new Congress convening on 3 Jan 2027.

Base case, in line with consensus, is that Democrats win at least one and more likely both houses of Congress. Prediction markets give Democrats better than 60% odds of sweeping and about 90% odds of winning the House.
The bigger the blue wave, the less likely post-election disruptions weigh on sentiment. If the blue wave fizzles, disruption risk and market volatility rise proportionally.
Markets are expected to look through most of the noise if the duration is short. Joined-up federal action is the key variable to track for markets.
Six out of 10 Americans say Trump will not accept the results if Democrats flip Congress. Trump has questioned election integrity on about 70% of his days back in office.

The highest-volatility Wave 1 event would be invocation of the Insurrection Act. Trump told Time on 1 Oct 2026 'I could use it'. Gold and non-USD safe havens would benefit, and a quick Supreme Court ruling or a narrowly targeted deployment could limit the volatility.

Wave 2 risks include federal agents seizing voting machines or ballots, federal warrants for election records, and prosecution threats against state election officials. Broken chain of custody could prevent state certification.

Wave 3 risks include a House Clerk omitting Democratic members-elect from the roll call, a defied court order to seat members, and a constitutional crisis. A bigger margin of victory makes gaming the process harder.

Republicans broadly support aggressive federal action: net +40pp support for federal seizure of voting machines or ballots after Election Day, which raises the odds of follow-through. Courts could slow such actions.

Trump's approval is at record lows. Iran war-driven fuel prices (diesel above $6/gal, gasoline above $4/gal at seasonal record highs) are driving voter frustration and putting red farm states in play.
Voters trust Democrats more than Republicans on the economy for the first time since 2010. Democrats lead on 10 of 13 issues and lead Republicans by about 10pp in voter enthusiasm.
Democrats have their own problem: more than half the electorate disapproves of both parties, and MAGA and democratic socialists are equally unpopular.
Republicans have a large cash edge, nearly 3x the Democrats if the MAGA Inc. super PAC is counted. Elon Musk has spent 3x the biggest known Democratic donor.

The Supreme Court's redistricting gift to Republicans has shrunk from a net 5-10 seats (June 2026) to 2-5 seats (Oct 2026). Recent Supreme Court losses for Trump include the September ruling on Postal Service mail-in ballot limits.

Concurrent risks before year-end: the Iran war, two Trump-Xi meetings (APEC Shenzhen 18-19 Nov, G20 Miami 14-15 Dec) that could be delayed, and a government shutdown if Congress fails to pass funding by 11 Dec. The US-China Busan trade detente expires 10 Jan.

TS Lombard expects Trump to escalate in order to de-escalate with Iran ahead of a more combative Congress. A changed Middle East should eventually help stabilize oil below the triple-digit zone. Six out of 10 voters say Trump will resume bombing Iran after the midterms.

Hedging view from Head of Strategy Daniel Von Ahlen: tactical long gold is the cleanest tail-risk hedge. Long VIX futures can play higher equity volatility, since spot VIX is low despite the chip sell-off and the term structure is flat relative to history.

tension_points.bull_case: Democrats are likely to win a large majority (60%+ sweep odds, ~90% House odds), making post-election disputes irrelevant to control, and markets look through short-lived noise. The AI trade could still benefit.
tension_points.bear_case: If the blue wave fizzles amid tight races and polling misses, disruption risk rises. Ambitious federal actions such as the Insurrection Act, seizing ballots or voting machines, or defying court orders could produce a prolonged crisis and volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A fizzled blue wave with tight House margins, or joined-up federal action such as invoking the Insurrection Act or seizing ballots before certification.
